content.user_title: Debug Code with Root Cause Discipline
content.value_statement: Bug fixes often fail when teams guess before they understand the cause. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through evidence-based debugging before implementation.
actual_capabilities: Structures debugging into root cause investigation, pattern analysis, hypothesis testing, and TDD implementation.
Requires complete error review, stable reproduction, recent change review, and data flow tracing before fixes.
Encourages comparison between working and broken examples to refine the root cause hypothesis.
Prompts one-variable hypothesis tests and stops after repeated failed fix attempts.
Provides a reusable bug analysis template with error details, reproduction notes, test results, and verification checks.
limitations: Does not execute diagnostics or repair code by itself.
Requires project context, error details, and reproduction steps from the user or repository.
Does not replace framework-specific debugging knowledge or official documentation.
Can slow down very small fixes when the root cause is already proven.

use_cases.title: Investigate a Regression
use_cases.description: Use the four-phase process to identify what changed, reproduce the failure, and verify the root cause before editing code.

use_cases.title: Review a Failed Fix Attempt
use_cases.description: Stop repeated trial-and-error changes and rebuild the investigation around one testable hypothesis.

use_cases.title: Document Production Bug Analysis
use_cases.description: Create a clear bug analysis record with evidence, comparisons, test results, and verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Start Root Cause Investigation
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a new bug report.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the flow-debugging process for this bug. First capture the full error, reproduction steps, recent changes, and data flow. Do not propose a fix yet.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Working and Broken Paths
prompt_templates.scenario: A reproduction exists but the cause is unclear.
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply Phase 2 of flow-debugging. Find similar working behavior, compare it with the failing path, and refine the root cause hypothesis with evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Test One Hypothesis
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Phase 3 of flow-debugging. Choose one testable hypothesis, design the smallest observation or test, and record what would confirm or reject it.

prompt_templates.title: Plan TDD Implementation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Phase 4 of flow-debugging. Define the failing test, the minimal fix, related regression checks, and the manual verification needed before completion.

output_examples.input: A checkout page fails only after a recent dependency update.
output: Root cause investigation lists the full error, exact reproduction path, and recent dependency commits.
Pattern analysis compares the checkout flow with another working payment flow.
Hypothesis testing isolates one dependency behavior before any fix is proposed.

output_examples.input: Three attempted fixes did not resolve a flaky test.
output: The workflow stops further guessing and reopens Phase 1.
The analysis records failed attempts, shared assumptions, and missing evidence.
A new single hypothesis is selected before another change is made.

output_examples.input: A confirmed parser bug needs an implementation plan.
output: The result defines a failing test that reproduces the parser issue.
The fix scope is limited to the confirmed root cause.
Verification includes the new test, related parser tests, and manual confirmation.

best_practices: Provide the complete error, stack trace, reproduction steps, and recent changes before asking for a fix.
Keep each hypothesis test focused on one variable so results are easy to interpret.
Write a failing test that reproduces the bug before implementing the final fix.
anti_patterns: Do not request a quick patch before the root cause is supported by evidence.
Do not change several files at once while testing a hypothesis.
Do not mark a bug resolved without regression tests and manual verification.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps AI assistants investigate software bugs systematically before suggesting or implementing fixes.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It describes a debugging process and may suggest read-only investigation steps for the assistant to perform.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it when a bug has unclear causes, repeated failed fixes, flaky behavior, or regression risk.

faq.question: Does it require test coverage?
faq.answer: It strongly prefers a failing test before implementation and verification tests after the fix.

faq.question: Can it replace framework documentation?
faq.answer: No. It organizes debugging work, but framework-specific facts still require project context and official references.

faq.question: Which assistants can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
